cosy-lesson.title: "If you want to know a person, discuss politics, religion, and women with him.": Fedor Dostoevsky

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Taboo – restricted by social custom or as a topic of polite conversation.

p.em: Example: In many cultures, talking about salary or personal beliefs remains strictly taboo.

cosy-blockquote.p: Controversy – prolonged public disagreement or heated debate.

p.em: Example: Political decisions often create intense controversy in local communities.

cosy-blockquote.p: Respect – due regard for the feelings, wishes, or traditions of others.

p.em: Example: It is possible to disagree completely on religious topics while maintaining mutual respect.

cosy-blockquote.p: Discussion – the action or process of talking about something in order to reach a decision or exchange ideas.

p.em: Example: A mature discussion requires active listening and an open mind.

cosy-blockquote.p: Character – the mental and moral qualities distinctive to an individual.

p.em: Example: How a person handles a political disagreement reveals their true character.

cosy-blockquote.p: Belief – an acceptance that a statement is true or that something exists.

p.em: Example: Our religious and moral beliefs are often shaped by our family background.

cosy-blockquote.p: Opinion – a view or judgment formed about something, not necessarily based on fact.

p.em: Example: In the digital age, everyone has a loud opinion on complex social issues.

cosy-blockquote.p: Dialogue – a conversation between two or more people directed toward agreement.

p.em: Example: Constructive political dialogue is rare when people are shouting at each other.

cosy-blockquote.p: Debate – a formal discussion on a particular topic in which opposing arguments are put forward.

p.em: Example: Watching a public debate can help you see different sides of an issue.

cosy-blockquote.p: Disagreement – a lack of consensus or approval; a dispute.

p.em: Example: A healthy relationship should allow for calm disagreement without fear of conflict.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Why does society establish taboo topics that are considered polite to avoid in public conversation?
★ Is there a topic that you consider completely taboo to discuss with colleagues?

How can we navigate intense social controversy without damaging our personal relationships?
★ Tell us about a recent controversy in the news that caught your attention.

How can we show genuine respect to someone whose fundamental values are opposite to ours?
★ Who in your life is best at showing respect during difficult discussions?

Why do family gatherings often dissolve into arguments when a political discussion begins?
★ Do you enjoy having intense political discussions with your family members?

Do you agree with Dostoevsky that discussing sensitive topics is the fastest way to understand a person's character?
★ What behavior in a discussion immediately reveals a person's character to you?

How should we handle situations where a close friend's religious belief conflicts with our moral values?
★ Has a close friend ever surprised you with an unexpected belief?

Why is it so easy to mistake a loud, unverified opinion for an objective fact on social media?
★ How comfortable are you saying 'I don't have enough information to form an opinion'?

What is the difference between winning an argument and engaging in a true, constructive dialogue?
★ When was the last time you had a truly eye-opening dialogue with someone?

Should high schools teach formal debate skills to help students learn how to argue logically?
★ Did you ever participate in a debate club or school competition?

Why does modern political culture view a simple disagreement as an act of personal hostility?
★ How has your personal handling of disagreement shifted over the last five years?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In a future world governed by total transparency, the concept of a social taboo will be completely eliminated. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How would you adapt if taboo became entirely obsolete in tomorrow's world?

The rapid speed of modern society will eventually make political controversy an obsolete concept. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you be willing to use technology to artificially boost your capacity for managing controversy?

Future educational systems will prioritize the cultivation of mutual respect over traditional academic success. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you want future generations of your family to remember your relationship with respect?

As artificial intelligence advances, machines will exhibit a superior capacity for philosophical discussion compared to humans. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could design a futuristic school, how would you teach the value of discussion to children?

In the coming decades, virtual character metrics will become a highly commercialized luxury commodity. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you fear a future where character is fully managed or monitored by digital algorithms?

The survival of human civilization will depend on our collective ability to practice shared belief systems. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you personally prepare for a future where personal belief is increasingly rare?

Future generations will look back at our current public opinion with deep skepticism. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could send a single message about public opinion to people living 100 years in the future, what would it be?

Global digital connectivity will make true constructive dialogue incredibly difficult to maintain in the future. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you choose to live in a futuristic utopia that completely guarantees peaceful dialogue at the cost of your freedom?

In the future, social status will be determined by a person's capacity for public debate rather than wealth. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What role do you hope debate will play in your own personal future over the next decade?

A world fully governed by logic will have no space left for the mystery of emotional disagreement. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If a machine could perfectly replicate your experience of disagreement, would you still value it?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation with teacher in 1-on-1 format.

ul.li: Incorrect: He have went to Paris → Correct: He has gone to Paris ((Present perfect third-person singular 'has' + past participle 'gone'.))

Incorrect: We discussed about the problem → Correct: We discussed the problem / had a discussion about the problem (('Discuss' is transitive and takes no preposition, or use 'have a discussion about'.))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Use 'agree' directly as a verb rather than using it with the auxiliary 'am'.))
